en: Mayon Volcano in Albay province is famous for its nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape among all Philippine volcanoes.
The Philippine tarsier, native to Bohol, is one of the world's smallest primates and has enormous eyes for night vision.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley before emptying into the Luzon Strait.
Lake Taal in Batangas is a unique freshwater lake containing Volcano Island, which itself holds a smaller main crater lake.
The Philippines is a top global producer of abaca, a banana plant whose strong natural fibers are woven into ropes and textiles.
Palawan is the largest province in the Philippines by total land area and is home to the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River.
The amihan is the cool northeast monsoon that brings dry, pleasant weather to the Philippines between November and February each year.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a protected UNESCO World Heritage site containing hundreds of coral species.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, lives in Mindanao and Luzon forests and is recognized by its distinctive shaggy head crest.
The Philippine Sea lies east of the archipelago and contains the Philippine Trench, one of the deepest oceanic trenches on Earth.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in the Cordillera region were carved into the mountains by the Ifugao people over two thousand years ago.
